page.text:
Cantor's diagonal argument illustrates the foundational discipline of the
chapter. The set $D$ exists by separation from $A$, not by unrestricted
comprehension. Its definition then converts the assumption that $f$ lists
every subset of $A$ into the contradiction $d\in D\iff d\notin D$ at a
purported index $d$ for $D$.
